title: Ephemeral-state-proxies-and-lightweight-tool-tokens-prd-wip
body:
Purpose

This doc proposes an approach for minimizing host-side state coupling and improving SDK ergonomics for tool-calling and structured streaming on unreliable or mobile networks. Core idea: introduce ephemeral-state proxies (lightweight stateless proxies that own session ephemeral IDs and minimal delta state) and short-lived tool tokens that allow clients to resume, replay, and validate partial tool interactions without pinning heavy session state in the control plane.

Why this is needed

- Many mobile and embedded clients face intermittent connectivity; full session snapshots are bulky and expensive to round-trip.
- Current streaming designs assume continuous TCP/WebSocket connections; reconnect and resume logic is ad-hoc across SDKs.
- Tool-calling (external actions) needs idempotency and replay semantics that are easy for app developers to reason about without deep server-side integration.
- We want a low-friction SDK experience: minimal config, predictable costs, and clear observability for partial/failed tool calls.

Goals

- Provide a resume-friendly streaming path with under-1s reconnect negotiation for clients on 3G/edge networks.
- Keep control-plane per-session state small (KBs) and ephemeral (TTL minutes).
- Surface a simple SDK API for starting/resuming sessions and issuing tool calls with automatic idempotency tokens.
- Ensure observability: every ephemeral session maps to persistent traceable artifacts in Console and logs.
- Maintain security posture: tool tokens scoped, auditable, and rotatable.

Non-goals

- This is not a full offline-first sync protocol (no local CRDT merging).
- Not attempting to replicate Dedicated/Private deployment networking models here; focus on hosted API and edge clients.

User stories

1) As a mobile app engineer, I want a single SDK call to start a streaming chat that can survive network blips without me writing complex reconnection code.
2) As a backend engineer, I want tool calls from clients to be idempotent so double-invocations caused by retries do not cause side-effect duplication.
3) As an SRE, I want ephemeral sessions to auto-expire and leave traceable audit records so we can debug partial outputs.

High-level design

Components:
- Ephemeral-state proxy (ESP): short-lived resource (session-id) created in control plane; stores small delta (last KV cache pointers, last tool-call metadata, last sequence number). ESPs are cheap to allocate, TTL-configurable (default 10m), and backed by a distributed cache.
- Lightweight tool tokens (LTT): short-lived JWT-like tokens minted per tool-call or per-session-tool-window. Tokens include tool id, idempotency nonce, scope (read/write), and expiration.
- SDK handshake: SDK requests new session -> control plane returns session-id + initial LTTs for client-side preflight. On reconnect, client presents session-id + last sequence number; control plane validates and issues resumed stream slot.

API sketch (textual)

- POST /v1/sessions
  body: { "model": "redwood-4-stream", "client_hint": "mobile-low-bandwidth" }
  response: { "session_id": "s_{...}", "ws_url": "wss://...", "initial_tool_tokens": [{"tool":"search","token":"t_...","expires":"..."}], "ttl_seconds": 600 }

- POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/resume
  body: { "last_seq": 123, "client_clock": 169... }
  response: { "resume_ok": true, "replay_instructions": "skip 122..123" }

- Tool call envelope (over stream or http):
  { "session_id":"s_...", "seq":124, "tool_token":"t_...", "tool_payload":{...} }

Idempotency and safety

- Tool tokens carry an idempotency nonce (client-supplied optional) and server-validated dedupe window.
- If a tool call is processed twice due to reconnect replay, control plane uses the tool_token+nonce to dedupe or route to a transactional proxy for side-effectful APIs.

SDK ergonomics

- SDK surfaces a single StreamingSession object. Key methods: start(), onPartial(), callTool(name, payload), resume(lastSeq), close().
- Automatic token refresh: SDK will transparently renew LTTs while session active; exposes hooks for token-expiry events for custom tooling.
- Developer ergonomics: default sensible retry/backoff, offline buffering up to configurable bytes, and best-effort optimistic local echo for UI.

Observability and Console mapping

- Every ephemeral session is represented in Console as a transient row (session id, client id, start_ts, ttl, last_seq, tool call summary) for last 24 hours by default.
- Traces show session creation, token issuance, each tool call attempt and dedupe outcomes.

Security model

- LTTs scoped to specific tool ids and operations. They are short-lived (default 2 minutes) to reduce blast radius.
- Audit logs persist tool token issuance and tool-call authorization events.
- Admins can revoke session ids and blacklist tokens via Console.

Metrics and success criteria

- Median session resume latency <= 1s in 90th percentile on mobile networks.
- Tool call duplication rate <= 0.1% after dedupe logic.
- Reduction in developer time to implement reconnection flows: measured via internal feedback from SDK beta users (target: 5x faster onboarding).

Rollout plan

- Phase 0 (internal alpha): implement ESP and LTT in control plane; provide Node/Typescript SDK prototype. 6 weeks.
- Phase 1 (beta): invite 10 customers (mobile-heavy) to test; integrate observability and token revocation. 8 weeks.
- Phase 2 (general availability): full SDKs (Python, Go, Java), Console UI, default TTL tuning. 4 weeks.

Open questions / trade-offs

- How large can ephemeral delta get before TTL eviction causes surprising replays? Need to cap stored delta and push larger state to persistent session snapshots.
- Token cadence: frequent small tokens reduce blast radius but increase token churn and issuance QPS on control plane. We should instrument QPS and set adaptive windows.
- Billing: ephemeral sessions should bill primarily on compute/ingress tokens used, not per-session TTL length. Need finance alignment.

Notes to reviewers

- This proposal tries to balance operational simplicity (statelessish control plane) with better client UX. Focus feedback on: token TTL defaults, SDK surface areas that feel heavyweight, and observability needs for debugging partial tool flows.

References and background

- Related threads: Slack #prod-streaming, notes in linked Confluence page.
- See INF-2147 for implementation ticket.
